item.title: ‘Will stand with Pakistan if US attacks’: Rajasthan BJP chief’s remark sparks Congress backlash
item.description: Rajasthan BJP president Madan Rathore stated that India would align with Pakistan in a potential US-Pakistan conflict. This statement has drawn significant criticism from Congress leaders, including Shama Mohamed. Mohamed questioned the BJP's stance and asked for clarification from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. Rathore also accused Rahul Gandhi of inciting unrest and mentioned foreign interference in India's stability.
item.dc:creator: Pallavi

item.title: SC Bar Association files criminal contempt plea against Sanjay Raut, Nikhil Wagle
item.description: Attorney General R Venkataramani has since granted consent to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against the two under the Contempt of Courts Act. The statements came after Chief Justice of India (CJI) declined a request last week from a delegation of opposition parties to meet him in person. The CJI said the delegation could instead file a petition before the court.

item.title: IGL rolls out AI system to check CNG cylinder safety at pumps
item.description: Indraprastha Gas Ltd has implemented an AI-enabled vehicle recognition system at various CNG stations in Delhi. This technology checks the hydrotest status of CNG cylinders to enhance safety measures. It ensures that vehicles with invalid certifications are alerted and refuelling is halted. The initiative follows a cylinder blast incident, prompting stricter enforcement of safety norms. The system will soon be deployed at all CNG stations managed by IGL.

item.title: Is Dhanush ready to make his political debut? Fan club's new avatar sparks buzz
item.description: Dhanush's fan club has evolved into the Dhanush Narpani Iyakkam, signaling possible political ambitions. The organization plans to set up local welfare units in five assembly constituencies within Coimbatore district. This transition involves the introduction of a new logo and flag, streamlining its identity. Although comparisons with Vijay's political path are inevitable, Dhanush has not made any official announcements regarding his political intentions, fueling speculation about his future moves.

item.title: Amit Shah vows to eliminate every trace of Naxalism after five decades of tribal suffering
item.description: Amit Shah highlighted the importance of eradicating Naxalism to restore growth in Bastar, Chhattisgarh. He noted that significant efforts had been made in this regard by local tribal leadership. Shah mentioned a distribution program of assistive devices benefiting over 3,600 disabled individuals, particularly Naxal violence victims. He emphasized the need to heal the wounds from years of suffering while maintaining that Naxalism's end does not restore dignity immediately.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Supreme Court seeks Centre’s response on plea to hold protest organisers liable for damage
item.description: The Supreme Court has requested responses regarding a plea to hold protest organizers accountable for damages. This includes potential liabilities for loss of life, injuries, and property damage incurred during protests. Additionally, the plea advocates for designated protest locations to minimize disturbances in densely populated areas. It proposes that protest organizers disclose their funding sources to ensure transparency.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: J&K HC restricts motorboat operations on Dal Lake
item.description: The high court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh has ordered a ban on fuel-powered motorboats and jet skis on Dal Lake. Authorities are directed to enforce this prohibition strictly to protect the lake from pollution. The court suggested exploring solar-powered boats as an alternative for tourism-related activities. Emergency services and safety operations are exempt from this ban. A comprehensive policy on motorised boat operations is expected for further review.

item.title: IMD announces onset of winter monsoon in south Peninsular India, summer monsoon withdrawal completes on normal date
item.description: The southwest monsoon in India withdrew on schedule. Simultaneously, the northeast monsoon commenced, bringing rainfall to parts of south Peninsular India. Regions including Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and coastal Andhra Pradesh experienced the initial winter rainfall. Predictions indicate a normal winter monsoon may provide relief after a significant summer rainfall deficit.
item.dc:creator: Vishwa Mohan

item.title: Ex-IAS Divya Mittal launches own party: 10 civil servants who quit service to enter politics
item.description: Divya Mittal, an ex-IAS officer, has established the Jan Neeti Bharat party in preparation for the forthcoming elections. With a focus on enhancing citizen participation in policymaking rather than adhering to conventional governance methods, she aims to make a significant impact. Her decision to retire after 13 years in civil service aligns with a trend of bureaucrats entering politics.
item.dc:creator: Pallavi

item.title: EC announces Special Summary Revision of voters' list in 17 states amid SIR row
item.description: While a Summary Revision focuses on new eligibles and routine corrections, SIR goes far deeper, involving statewide house-to-house verification, detailed scrutiny of entries, and large-scale data audits. For instance, under a Summary Revision, a voter who has shifted homes must file a form to update their address. Under SIR, the Booth Level Officer visits that address, confirms whether the voter still lives there, checks if anyone new has become eligible, and updates the roll based on physical verification rather than waiting for the voter to initiate the change.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Lula or Bolsonaro: Why Brazil's presidential election matters for Brics and India
item.description: Brics began with five members and grew to eleven after the 2024 expansion, with Indonesia the newest, joining in 2025. Brazil opposed the enlargement, particularly because of the one nation. Iran. It feared that adding the avowedly anti-West Islamic Republic would cost the group its cohesion. Like India, Brazil wants Brics to be reformist and not revolutionary, thereby limiting it to a body that argues for change inside the existing order rather than one that tries to replace it.
